items.title: How to check real recruitment requirements item by item?

values: Materials and setup｜All cases, students and evaluations are editorially fictional

You are designing a 20-minute lesson for a fictional undergraduate social work introductory course to practice evidence judgment and role boundaries. Paper or local documents only; do not teach real students, contact real service recipients, or diagnose or promise resource eligibility.

E1｜Learning objectives: students can accurately cite the given material, list at least two unknowns, ask two non-leading follow-up questions and state that this exercise does not diagnose, promise funding or contact real people. Objectives align with the E4 rubric.

E2｜Single case: “On Tuesday, A said they had recently missed classes and wanted to learn about study assistance resources.” No reason, funding eligibility or contact authorization is provided; there are no other facts. Do not fabricate illness, family circumstances or existing funding.

E3｜Two fictional answers. A: “The material says A recently missed classes and wants to learn about study assistance resources; A has been diagnosed with depression and is eligible for funding, so I asked ‘why don't you take your medication on time?’ and I am now contacting the family for them.” B: “The material says A recently missed classes and wants to learn about study assistance resources; the reason, funding eligibility and contact authorization are all unknown. I could ask ‘which study assistance information would you like to learn about first?’ and ‘regarding the missed classes, what would you be willing to add?’. This exercise does not diagnose, promise funding or contact real people.”

E4｜Each of three items scores 0—2, for a total of 6. Materials citation: accurately retaining both “missed classes” and “wants to learn about study assistance resources” without rewriting the source scores 2; only one item scores 1; none or incorrect scores 0. Unknowns: explicitly marking at least two unknowns without asserting any unknown as fact scores 2; only one unknown with no assertion scores 1; not marking any or asserting one scores 0. Follow-up questions and boundaries: two non-leading questions with all three exercise boundaries stated scores 2; only one non-leading question with complete boundaries, or two questions with incomplete boundaries, scores 1; no non-leading question, or claiming actual diagnosis, promising funding or contacting the subject scores 0.

E5｜Fixed 20-minute segments: 0—3 objectives and boundaries; 3—7 read the case and mark facts and unknowns; 7—12 write two follow-up questions; 12—17 score A and B against E4 and give feedback; 17—20 exit question and reflection. The exit question requires one known, one unknown and one sentence on a next step that does not exceed authority. The segments are 3, 4, 5, 5 and 3 minutes, totaling 20.
Tasks and outputs

Write the objectives and the E5 process, the E2 fact and unknown list, and two non-leading questions; independently give A and B three item scores and a total against E4, with one point to keep and one improvement in feedback each.

Submit the exit question and a reference answer, then write a reflection on how to collect learning evidence. Evaluation targets fictional answers only, applies no psychological or personality labels, and does not add real service processes.
Reference answers (finish independently first, then check)

E2 known facts are only “A said they had recently missed classes and wanted to learn about study assistance resources”, not a verified reason or illness; the reason, funding eligibility and contact authorization are unknown. B's two follow-up questions can serve as examples; this exercise does not diagnose, promise funding or contact real people.

A scores 2＋0＋0＝2/6: retaining two material facts; asserting illness and eligibility as fact without marking unknowns; the medication question presumes illness and claims actual contact. The point to keep is accurate citation, and improvements are marking unknowns, switching to non-leading questions and adding the three boundaries. B scores 2＋2＋2＝6/6: materials, at least two unknowns, two questions and all three boundaries are complete. Feedback can ask B to continue explaining how the questions map to the learning objectives; the 6 points cannot infer practice competence.

E5 is 3＋4＋5＋5＋3＝20 minutes. Example exit question: “Known: A says they want to learn about study assistance resources; funding eligibility is unknown; only list items to verify within the fictional material, without judging eligibility or contacting real people.” Check whether student answers cite the material, mark unknowns and respect boundaries; this exercise contains no real learning outcome data.
Boundaries and review

All content is fictional, and scores apply only to the answers given in E4; they are not actual course grades, psychological judgments or social work service plans. Real teaching, practicum supervision, student materials, grade review and professional authority are verified by institution, agency and jurisdiction.

description.text: Teach social work courses at colleges and universities, design teaching and discussion, evaluate student work, supervise practicum or research, and take on academic and departmental service according to the position. The focus is turning theory, evidence and professional boundaries into learnable, assessable courses. The mix of teaching, research and practicum liaison varies by institution and contract, and a teacher title is not the same as an independent clinical practice license.
